chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Haytham ibn Abī Masrūq, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
"If two drains were flowing, one drain with urine and one drain with water, and they mixed, then if it touched you, there would be no harm in it."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The correct way of understanding these two reports is that rainwater, when it flows from the drainpipe, has the ruling of flowing water; nothing renders it najis except that which changes its color, taste, or smell. This indicates that.

key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْجَارِي: flowing water, which has a distinct rule in fiqh regarding najasah
key_terms.بَوْلٍ: urine, mentioned here as an impurity
key_terms.رَائِحَتَهُ: its smell, one of the signs of change affecting purity
key_terms.لَوْنَهُ: its color, one of the signs of change affecting purity
key_terms.مَاءٍ: water, specifically in the context of purification law
key_terms.مَاءَ الْمَطَرِ: rainwater, treated here under a specific legal ruling
key_terms.مِيزَابٌ: a drainpipe or spout through which water flows
key_terms.يُنَجِّسُهُ: renders it najis or ritually impure

ai.seo_question: Does rainwater flowing from a drain become najis if it mixes with urine?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the fiqh ruling of rainwater flowing through a drain and mixing with impurity. It explains that such water takes the ruling of flowing water, which is not rendered najis unless its color, taste, or smell changes. The report is significant in discussions of ritual purity and the laws governing water in Shia jurisprudence.
